solutions.check: clues read from the FT's printable PDF (PDF has no vector grid), the grid backsolved from their numbering, the one grid that fits; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Shoot convict exhibiting sickness from being transported

parts.note: to shoot out is to jet, as water from a hose
a lag is slang for a convict, especially an old lag

explanation.surface: A firing squad dispatches a prisoner who is showing signs of illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transported' suggests the convict deported to Australia, but it means air travel across time zones.
explanation.definitionFit: Jet lag is the tiredness and malaise caused by flying across several time zones.

clue.text: Stumble and trip

parts.note: to err is to make a mistake, to stumble
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone falls over and goes flying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trip' looks like a stumble but is the noun, a short journey.
explanation.definitionFit: An errand is a short journey made to deliver or collect something.

clue.text: Revealing almost new intrusion into mixed wedlock

indicators.note: an intrusion pushes one thing inside another, so the short piece goes within
mixed means these letters are jumbled together
almost means the word falls just short, losing its final letter

explanation.surface: A suggestion that a new intrusion into a mixed marriage is exposing.
explanation.walkthrough: NE (new without its last letter) goes into a jumble of WEDLOCK.
explanation.definitionFit: A dress cut low at the neck is revealing, showing much of the chest.

clue.text: Thousands go on strike in major event

indicators.note: one piece goes on after the other, so they are put side by side

parts.note: a grand is slang for a thousand pounds or dollars
to lam is to beat or hit hard

explanation.surface: Thousands of workers walk out in a large industrial action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go on strike' reads as a walkout, but 'strike' alone means hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand slam is winning all the major tournaments in a sport such as tennis or golf.

clue.text: Stir milk and oats together

definitions.meaning: stir is British slang for prison, and doing a stretch inside is also called by this name
oats cooked in milk make the breakfast dish

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction to stir the milk and oats in the pan.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb 'Stir' looks like part of a recipe, but it is a noun meaning prison; doing time is known by the same word in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Oatmeal boiled in milk or water is this breakfast dish; it is also British slang for a prison sentence.

clue.text: No time to pick a hot recipe for cabbage

indicators.note: a recipe combines ingredients anew, so the letters are mixed
no means the following item is dropped from the letters

explanation.surface: A cook picks a spicy dish for cabbage without much time.
explanation.walkthrough: Take T out of PICKAHOT, then rearrange PICKAHO.
explanation.definitionFit: Pak choi is a Chinese cabbage with dark leaves and white stalks.

clue.text: It's sticky to misbehave once more

parts.note: re- is a prefix meaning again
to sin is to do wrong

explanation.surface: It is a tricky business to behave badly again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sticky' looks like awkward, but it describes a gummy substance.
explanation.definitionFit: Resin is a sticky substance exuded by trees such as pines.

clue.text: Home help raised in Asian country

parts.note: being at home is being in

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: aid is help

explanation.surface: Domestic staff brought up in an Asian country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Home help' looks like a single domestic helper, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: India is a large nation in South Asia.

clue.text: Gorilla, perhaps, to feed with skin of fruit

indicators.note: the fruit forms a skin round the outside of the next piece

parts.note: a grape is a fruit
to feed is to eat

explanation.surface: A gorilla eating with the peel of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The gorilla is an example of the great apes, along with chimpanzees and orangutans.

clue.text: This could be a clue to ward's handicap

parts.note: the word ward written back to front gives draw, so ward is what you get from draw read back

explanation.surface: A puzzle hint about some hospital ward and its disadvantage.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer, read as an instruction, says to write draw backwards, and that gives the clue word 'ward'.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawback is a disadvantage or hindrance, just as a handicap is.

clue.text: Muddy grass bordering nest

indicators.note: one piece sits right beside the next, touching it at its edge, so they are joined side by side

parts.note: sod is turf, a piece of grass with its soil
a den is a lair or nest for an animal

explanation.surface: Mud-covered turf lying around the edge of a bird's nest.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground that is soaked through and waterlogged is both sodden and muddy.

clue.text: Quite at home with daring exploit

parts.note: someone at home is said to be in
a deed is a feat, often a heroic one

explanation.surface: Someone is perfectly comfortable with a bold adventure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quite' is the agreeing reply, as in 'Quite!', meaning yes, exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are emphatic replies of agreement, as in 'Quite so' and 'Yes, really'.

clue.text: One last night of debauchery, then pray for rehabilitation

indicators.note: rehabilitation remakes something into a new form, so these letters are rebuilt

explanation.surface: A reveller has a final wild night out, then repents and prays to be reformed.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride-to-be's celebration with her friends is traditionally a final night of excess before marriage.

clue.text: Discharge Manx cat?

indicators.note: Manx cats have no tail, so the word loses its tail letter

parts.note: puss is a familiar word for a cat

explanation.surface: Asking whether a tailless cat from the Isle of Man is being let go.
explanation.definitionFit: Pus is the yellowish matter discharged from an infected wound.

clue.text: Diverse variety of sights as epic looked for rejuvenation

indicators.note: rejuvenation gives something a new form, so these letters are recast

explanation.surface: A tired old epic is revived and looks fresh, with many different scenes.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, a kaleidoscope is a constantly changing pattern or a varied mixture of things.

clue.text: Flip contents in clear out

indicators.note: in places the middle piece within the outer word

parts.note: obvious means clear or plain

indicators.note: the contents are the inside letters, without the outer ones

explanation.surface: An instruction to flip over and clear out a container's contents.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone out of it or unaware of their surroundings is oblivious.

clue.text: Disturbed at a curlew's screech

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown into disorder, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A wading bird that has been startled lets out a shriek.
explanation.definitionFit: To caterwaul is to make a shrill howling cry like a cat; here the noun sense, a screech.

clue.text: Fraction split tax period

indicators.note: a word that is split has another piece put in its gap

parts.note: to dun is to press a debtor for payment, a sense close to tax
a ratio is a fraction

explanation.surface: Part of a tax payment divided over a period.
explanation.definitionFit: A duration is a length of time, a period.

clue.text: Exploding slug sounds doubly stupid when hit by train

indicators.note: the first piece is struck by the next, which follows it in the answer
doubly here means the synonym for stupid is written out twice
the word sounds tells us to say the next phrase and write what we hear

parts.note: dumb means stupid
a bullet train is a high-speed train, as on Japan's Shinkansen

explanation.surface: A slow creature stupid enough to be run over by a train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slug' looks like the garden creature but is slang for a bullet; a dumdum is one that expands on impact.
explanation.definitionFit: A dumdum is an expanding bullet, and slug is slang for any bullet.

clue.text: Make noise in vessel

indicators.note: noise points to how a word is heard, not how it is spelt

parts.note: to make money is to earn it

explanation.surface: Someone bangs about in a container.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the two words sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: An urn is a vase or large container, as for tea or ashes.

clue.text: Even extracts from quinoa and birdseed are combined without any help

indicators.note: even extracts are the letters in the 2nd, 4th and 6th places of each word

explanation.surface: A health food mix of quinoa and birdseed blended together, made by oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Done alone, without assistance, means unaided.

clue.text: Men were killed when thrown together

parts.note: soldiers who fell in battle were killed
as can mean when, as in as I left

explanation.surface: People thrown together when some died.
explanation.definitionFit: Fellas is informal for men or chaps.

clue.text: Excerpt from essay on a Rabelaisian farewell

indicators.note: Excerpt from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A passage from an essay on a bawdy writer in the style of Rabelais, bidding goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a Japanese word for goodbye, used in English as a farewell.

clue.text: It hurts to go along with baby bird

parts.note: ow is a cry of pain
to let something happen is to allow it, to go along with it

explanation.surface: It is painful to be a young bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The suffix -let marks a small or young one, so this is the term for a young owl, a fledgling.

clue.text: Abroad, a measure of acidity in alcohol?

parts.note: ale is an alcoholic drink
pH is the scale measuring acidity

explanation.surface: Wondering abroad about the acidity level in alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abroad, a' defines the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, the equivalent of our A.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleph is the Hebrew counterpart of the letter A.

clue.text: Green at former girlfriend's crown

parts.note: vert is the heraldic word for green
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: Someone envious looks at the jewellery of a former partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' looks like envy, but it is heraldry, where green is named vert.
explanation.definitionFit: The vertex is the highest point or top of something, as the crown of the head is.

clue.text: Part of fish that is a guide for anglers

parts.note: a gill is the breathing organ of a fish
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A fishing guide points out part of the fish they have caught.
explanation.walkthrough: A gillie (or ghillie) is a Scottish attendant who guides people on hunting or fishing trips.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland the term names a man who attends sportsmen fishing or stalking on an estate.

clue.text: It's crazy to fool around outside mirrored toilet

indicators.note: the first word wraps round the outside of the next piece, holding it

parts.note: to dally is to fool about or trifle

indicators.note: a mirror shows things back to front, so the word is read from the right

parts.note: loo is British informal for a toilet

explanation.surface: Someone acts the fool by messing about in front of the bathroom mirror.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fool around' suggests messing about, but it is the verb to dally, which wraps round the toilet word turned back.
explanation.definitionFit: Doolally is British slang, from army use in India, for mad or out of one's mind.

clue.text: Caught snippet of music with adjacent notes

parts.note: a snatch is a brief fragment of a song or tune
E and D sit side by side in the musical scale

explanation.surface: Someone hears a fragment of a tune with neighbouring notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Snatched means grabbed or seized quickly, as when something is caught.

clue.text: Reduce power to interior of display

indicators.note: one letter is placed within the inside of the next word, so it goes in

parts.note: to slash prices is to cut them sharply
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: An instruction to dim the power to the inside of a display case.
explanation.definitionFit: A splash is a showy display, as in a newspaper's big front-page story.
